title: terraform: private GPU node pools + IAM/networking state layout update
author: Diego Morales
description: Motivation: private deployments need a clearer Terraform state layout for GPU node pools, IAM roles, and networking so teams can perform safe upgrades and scale node pools independently across environments/regions. This PR restructures Terraform modules and state layout: 1) factor node pools into a dedicated module with per-environment state targeting, 2) introduce explicit IAM role modules for node pool service accounts and node driver permissions, 3) expose networking artifacts (subnet IDs, route tables, NAT gateways) from the networking module to the private-installer module for deterministic references, and 4) add a documented migration path (terraform state mv/import commands + verification plan). The change also includes a backwards-compatible rollout plan (canary apply to staging, full apply with drain/cordon strategy) and a rollback procedure. Checklist: - [x] Module refactor (node_pools, iam, networking) - [x] State layout and backend config updates - [x] Migration guide and automated helper script (scripts/tf-migrate.sh) - [x] CI: terraform fmt/validate/plan integration - [x] Tests: integration plan against staging infra - [x] Docs: upgrade notes for customers and SREs Related: ENG-1423 (Node pool isolation), INF-208 (Private installer state hygiene). Notes on risk: state movement requires operator intervention; included idempotent helpers and a dry-run plan. See migration steps and rollback at the end of this description. Migration summary: - Move existing node_pool resources into module namespace: terraform state mv module.redwood_node_pool.google_container_node_pool.redwood_gpu_pool module.node_pools.google_container_node_pool.gpu_pool - Import newly created IAM roles where missing: terraform import module.iam.google_service_account.node_pool_sa projects/REDACTED/serviceAccounts/node-pool-sa@... - Validate plan in staging then apply to production during scheduled maintenance window. Rollback: revert to previous state file backup and re-import resources if an apply fails and nodes cannot be reconciled. This PR intentionally avoids changing compute instance types and focuses on layout and IAM/network references so no runtime traffic impact is expected during planning steps.

release_notes: Restructure Terraform state for private deployments: node pools extracted to dedicated module, IAM roles for node pool service accounts added, networking module now exposes subnet/route outputs. Migration helpers and docs included. Operators must follow the documented migration steps when upgrading. No runtime model changes included.
migration_guide: See docs/upgrade/migrate-nodepools.md and scripts/tf-migrate.sh. High level: 1) run scripts/tf-migrate.sh --dry-run and review plan 2) backup current state 3) run provided terraform state mv commands 4) plan against new backend and import missing IAM or networking resources 5) apply to staging and verify node registration 6) apply to production during maintenance window. If problems: restore state snapshot and run rollback/import steps.
notes: This PR prioritizes operator clarity over schema compactness. We avoided changing compute sizes or autoscaler thresholds in this change to reduce blast radius. Follow-up is scheduled to add automated imports and more granular per-region state backends.
